short: every row of one table paired with every row of another: n × m rows. every join starts from it, on paper.
a join whose ON is an = between a column on each side. the common case, and the only one a venn diagram tries to draw.
the pairs of rows where ON is true, and nothing else. a row with no partner is left out.
a join condition written as shared column names: USING (dept) means ON a.dept = b.dept, with dept output once.
a join on every column name the two tables share, worked out when the query runs. fragile: a new column changes it.
an inner join plus the rows that matched nothing, from one side (LEFT, RIGHT) or both (FULL), padded with NULLs.
the NULLs an outer join puts in the other table's columns for a row that found no partner. nobody stored them.
a table joined to itself under two aliases, so a row can meet another row of the same table, like an employee and their manager.
a one-to-many join repeating the one side once per match, so sums, counts and averages over it come out inflated.
what one row of a result stands for: one order, one order line, one customer. a sum is only right at its own grain.
a SELECT in parentheses, used where a value or a table can go.
a subquery that returns one value: one column, at most one row. more rows is an error, none is NULL.
a subquery in FROM, used as a table for one query. postgres 16 made its alias optional.
a subquery that uses a column of the outer query, so it gets a new answer for every outer row.
keep each left row once if at least one right row matches. written EXISTS or IN, it never duplicates rows.
keep the left rows that match no right row at all. written NOT EXISTS, or a LEFT JOIN keeping only padded rows.
the rows related to every member of a set, like students who took every CS course. a double NOT EXISTS, or a count.
x NOT IN (subquery) returns no rows at all when the subquery returns a NULL, because x <> NULL is never true.
lets a subquery or function in FROM use columns of the tables to its left, so it runs once per left row.
UNION, INTERSECT or EXCEPT: two results with the same columns, stacked or compared row by row.
both results, one after the other, duplicates kept. no hashing or sorting, so it's the cheap one.
common table expression: a subquery named in WITH at the top of a statement, usable like a table below it.
a CTE computed once into a temporary result that the query reads. the default when it's used twice, or forced with MATERIALIZED.
